check.title: Circuit check

led-no-series-resistor.title: LED with no series resistor
led-no-series-resistor.why: Nothing limits the current through the LED, so it draws far more than it should.
led-no-series-resistor.fix: Put a resistor in series with the LED.

led-reversed.title: LED the wrong way round
led-reversed.why: An LED only conducts one way. Here it faces backwards, so no current flows.
led-reversed.fix: Turn the LED so the long leg faces the positive side.

output-contention.title: Two outputs fighting
output-contention.why: Two pins drive the same net to different levels, so they push against each other.
output-contention.fix: Drive the net from one output only, or make the other pin an input.

supply-shorted-to-ground.title: Supply shorted to ground
supply-shorted-to-ground.why: A path with almost no resistance joins the supply to ground, so the current is huge.
supply-shorted-to-ground.fix: Remove the direct connection between the supply and ground.

floating-input.title: Floating input
floating-input.why: An input pin is connected to nothing, so it picks up noise and reads random levels.
floating-input.fix: Tie the pin to a known level with a pull-up or pull-down.

part-not-powered.title: Part not powered
part-not-powered.why: The part has no supply voltage on its power pin, so it does nothing.
part-not-powered.fix: Connect the power pin to the supply.

button-no-pulldown.title: Button with no pull-down
button-no-pulldown.why: The button input has no resistor to a known level, so it floats when the button is open.
button-no-pulldown.fix: Add a pull-down resistor, or turn on the pull-up in code.

open-connection.title: Open connection
open-connection.why: A wire or leg does not reach its target, so the path is broken.

swapped-pins.title: Swapped pins
swapped-pins.why: Two pins are connected to each other's places, so signals arrive at the wrong pins.
swapped-pins.fix: Connect each pin to its own place.

wrong-value.title: Wrong value
wrong-value.why: A part has a value that does not suit the circuit, so the result is off.
wrong-value.fix: Use the value the circuit needs.

missing-ground.title: Missing ground
missing-ground.why: The circuit has no connection back to ground, so no current can complete its loop.
missing-ground.fix: Connect the ground pin to the ground rail.

wrong-pin-in-code.title: Wrong pin in code
wrong-pin-in-code.why: The code uses a different pin number from the one the part is wired to.
wrong-pin-in-code.fix: Use the pin number the part is wired to.

i2c-missing-pullup.title: I2C pull-up missing
i2c-missing-pullup.why: The I2C lines have no pull-up resistors, so they never rise to a high level.
i2c-missing-pullup.fix: Add a pull-up resistor from each I2C line to the supply.

pin-overcurrent.title: Pin overcurrent
pin-overcurrent.why: A pin supplies more current than it can safely give.
pin-overcurrent.fix: Drive the load through a transistor, or use a larger resistor.

brownout.title: Brown-out
brownout.why: The supply sags under load, so the board resets or misbehaves.
brownout.fix: Power the load from a separate supply, or reduce the load.

reverse-polarity.title: Reverse polarity
reverse-polarity.fix: Connect positive to positive and negative to negative.

bus-device-not-modelled.title: Bus device not modelled
bus-device-not-modelled.why: A device on the bus has no model yet, so it cannot answer here.
bus-device-not-modelled.fix: Check the wiring and code against the datasheet; this simulator cannot show the device.

library-not-modelled.title: Library not modelled
library-not-modelled.why: The sketch uses a library the simulator does not model, so its calls have no effect.
library-not-modelled.fix: Test the library on a real board.

x-code.serial-baud-mismatch.title: Serial baud mismatch
x-code.serial-baud-mismatch.why: The sketch and the monitor use different baud rates, so the text is garbled.
x-code.serial-baud-mismatch.fix: Set the same baud rate in both.

x-code.pin-mode-wrong.title: Pin mode wrong
x-code.pin-mode-wrong.why: The pin is used as an output or an input but was set up the other way.
x-code.pin-mode-wrong.fix: Call pinMode with the mode the code needs.

symptom.i2c-no-ack: The device does not answer on I2C
symptom.pin-level-wrong: A pin shows the wrong level

wiring.1: Follow the signal from the source to the part.
wiring.3: Check what pin {pin} of {part} is connected to.

power.1: Think about where the power comes from and where it goes back.
power.2: Look at the supply and ground around {part}.
power.3: Check the voltage on {net}; it should be about {expected} {unit}.

code.1: Compare what the code says with what the circuit does.
code.2: Look at the lines of code that touch {part}.
code.3: Check which pin the code uses for {part}, and how that pin is set up.

bus.1: Think about what the two ends of the bus need.
bus.2: Look at the bus lines that reach {part}.
bus.3: Check the lines on {net} and what they are connected to.

value.1: Think about whether the numbers suit the part.
value.3: Check that {value} {unit} suits {part}; about {expected} {unit} is expected.
